unit.why: A single tale told by R. Yitzhak of Neskhiz. An old market woman sees her dead husband fumigating the road for the tzaddikim of the Holy Land, who are coming to greet the soon-to-die Apter Rav, and the Apter dies two days later.

stories.start_quote: סיפר הרה״ק מהר"י מנעסכיז שאשה זקינה אחת
stories.end_quote: וסיים הרה״ק מנעסכיז זו מעשה יפה
stories.summary_en: A poor widow sees her late husband running, either awake or in a dream. He explains that he was smoking the road to purify the air for the tzaddikim of the Land of Israel coming to receive the Apter Rav, and promises her livelihood. The Apter, still healthy on Tuesday, dies on Thursday.

tags.why: Framed as a tale told by the Neskhizer rebbe, who ends it with 'this is a fine story'.

quotes: איני יודע אם בהקיץ או בחלום ראיתי את בעלי
tags.why: The woman is unsure whether she saw her husband awake or in a dream.

quotes: ראיתי את בעלי ע"ה שנפטר זה כמה שנים
tags.why: She has a possibly waking sight of her dead husband.

quotes: ובשובו אמר לי הנה מעתה יהי' לך פרנסה
tags.why: She converses with the soul of her deceased husband.

quotes: לקבל פני האפטער שיפטר מהעולם בקרוב
tags.why: The imminent death of the Apter is foretold and comes true.
The arc runs from prediction to fulfilment, though here the predictor is a dead soul rather than a tzaddik.
The death of the Apter Rav is depicted.
The story centres on the heavenly preparations for the Apter's death.

quotes: אשה זקינה אחת שהיתה יושבת בשוק
tags.why: The widow is the seer and first-person narrator of the vision.

quotes: זה הי' ביום ג׳ ואז הי' האפטער בבריאותו
tags.why: The meaning of the vision becomes clear only after the Apter dies.

quotes: הנה הנחתני עם יתומים בחוסר פרנסה
tags.why: The widow weeps over her destitution.

departed tzaddikim coming to receive a dying tzaddik's soul
widowhood and livelihood (parnasa) promised from beyond
